text:
Nigeria minister of power Joseph Tegbe don assure kontri pipo say electricity supply go improve within 48 to 72 hours as govment don begin work to address wetin dey responsible for recent outages in parts of the country.
Oga Tegbe assurance dey as some parts of di kontri dey experience blackout and odas dey experience epileptic power supply.
Some areas for Lagos neva see power supply in weeks, while some wey dey see am tok say serious drop don dey for how dem dey get light, and dem don begin question wetin dey cause di unstable supply.
Di minister of power for one statement on Saturday explain say, part of wetin dey cause di worsening electricity situation na sake of one maintenance dem plan to carry out for di Egbin Power Station.
Egbin power station na Nigeria "largest" thermal power generating station for Lagos, wey dey supply about 16% of di total electricity on di national grid.

Oga Tegbe also say limited of gas supplies to some thermal power stations don reduce di amount of electricity wey di national grid get".
To solve di kasala, di statement reveal say, "grid operators don implement load shedding for some areas to fit manage di shortfall".
Di power minister also blam di spoiling of some of di koko transition routes na im don block supply tome areas, especially for Lagos.
Nigeria Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe don torchlight di lack of light wey kontri pipo dey face say dem go fix am within three days.
Di Honourable Minister tok dis one for statement wia e reveal say di light mata dey affect four states wey include Lagos and Abuja.
Oga Tegbe list di reasons wey light no dey as bicos of "planned maintenance Egbin Power Station and di wahala for gas supplies to some thermal powet stations. Dis don reduce di amount of electricity wey di national grid get".
To solve di kasala, di statement reveal say, "grid operators don implement loaf shedding for some areas to fit manage di shortfall".
Di power minister also blam di spoiling of some of di koko transition routes na im don block supply tome areas, especially for Lagos.
Minister Tegbe promse say power go return to some places within three days as im promise for im statement say, "my team and me dey work to return di affected generationg units to service in phases. Di first units go come back online within di next 48 to 72 hours".
E also reveal say, "we also dey tok wit operators to helep improve gas supply and ginger do repairs for damaged infrastructure".
Im tok-tok link wit wetin di Nigerian Independent System Operator, Niso tok about di light situation for di kontri.
For statement wey dem release on Thursday, dem blame di reduction in electricty generation for di national grid to two tins, wey be wahala in di gas supply to di thermal power generating stations and di reduced output wey dey comot from di hydroelectric power stations.
Dem explain say, "Limited gas supply don reduce di amount of electricity wey some thermal power stations fit generate, while low water levels for dams don also affect hydroelectric power generation. Bicos of dis, less electricity dey available for Distribution Companies (DisCos) to carry give consumers. Di result be say people dey experience fewer hours of light and more load shedding for different areas."
Even di Transmission Company of Nigeria add dia mouth inside di mata of light outage afta one of di DisCos bin blame dem for lack of light.
On Firday, dem tok say, "TCN say the claim wey Ikeja Electric (IKEDC) make say "grid instability" cause some recent power outages no correct.
"TCN explain say na only NISO get power to tok wetin really cause problems for di national grid, and NISO don alreadi explain say di main problem na lack of enough gas for some power plants and low water levels for hydro dams. Bicos of dis, less electricity dey generated and less power dey available for distribution."
Dem add say, "TCN say di outages no happen bicos transmission equipment spoil. According to di records, most of the interruptions happen because power generation reduce, while some odas happun because of issues on IKEDC's own network and because IKEDC no follow some load allocation instructions.
"TCN also point out say some feeders wey IKEDC mention, including MTN, Iju Water Works and Rack Centre, get faults from IKEDC network itself. For example, di Rack Centre outage on 2 November happun bicos of cable fault for IKEDC network, and na IKEDC workers repair am."
TCN say blaming them for power shortages wey come from low electricity generation dey give customers wrong information. Dem advise IKEDC and other DisCos to always use verified information from NISO when explaining power supply problems to customers."
Signing di Electricity Act, 2023 on June 9 - Di act liberalise and deregulate di power sector, wey move am from di exclusive list so dat states and sub nationals go fit participate for power generation, distribution, and transmission wey states like Lagos, Enugu, Abia, Ekiti, Oyo, Kaduna and Niger dey take advantage of.
President Tinubu bin take ova N6 trillion legacy debt wey bin accumulate from 2015 to 2025.
E start di Presidential Metering Initiative to close di ova 7 million Metering gap.
Dele Alake add say in di last three years, ova 1.5 million customers don receive meter under di Presidential Metering Initiative.
Di Rural Electrification Agency don also connect universities, hospitals, and rural communities to solar power.
Di administration create N4 trillion bond programme to settle verified legacy debts to 21 power generating companies (Gencos) and gas companies (Gascos).
E say dem still dey fix di electricity market and power sector and President Tinubu neva comot one inch from im commitment.
Wetin Nigerians dey face be say, for some states and areas light dey while some oda parts no dey too get light.
Di national grid still dey collapse up and down, for 2026 alone, e collapse pass six times and Nigerians still dey ask why National Grid dey collapse evritime
Nigeria for some areas dey use meter, while some pipo still dey use estimated billing.
